sections.title: Type notes for the app's imports
sections.what: Declares how the editor should understand the style imports and the diagram library imports, including the one diagram stylesheet import.
sections.why: Likely reason: the editor does not know about these imports by default.
sections.watch_out: The diagram library's declared version may not match the one installed or used.

summary: Tells the editor how to handle imports of style files and the React Flow diagram library so the code type-checks.
purpose: Declares the types for imports the editor does not know on its own.
why: Likely reason: without these notes, the editor would report errors on imports that work fine when the app runs.
how: It loads Vite's standard type notes, declares that CSS imports are text records, declares the diagram package as coming from the older react-flow-renderer package, and declares the diagram stylesheet import.
outputs: Type information used only by the editor and the type checker.
risks: The diagram declaration points to the older react-flow-renderer package, while package.json also lists newer @reactflow packages. The packet does not show which one the diagram code imports, so the types may not match the code that actually runs.
debug: If the editor says a module cannot be found, check this file. If diagram types look wrong, compare package.json with the diagram file's imports.
